author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human for workspace-architectural sign-off. JMAP-x2gd.4 and JMAP-x2gd.3 (SpaceInvite manage_members enforcement) are the same shape: both need backend-canonical permission gates atomic with the create/destroy mutation. The bead description offers three paths; all three require either (a) new ChatBackend trait methods, (b) extending apply_space_patch with new variants, or (c) a may_* gate hook in conjunction with backend create_object re-check. None of the three is a small change; all touch the public ChatBackend trait surface plus MemoryBackend plus the 3 test fixture backends (FaultyBackend, IdentityBackend, TrackingBackend).

Options considered:

(A) Add 4 typed methods to ChatBackend: create_space_ban, destroy_space_ban, create_space_invite, destroy_space_invite. Each performs the permission gate atomically with the write. Handlers call the typed method instead of the generic create_object/destroy_object. Default impl returns forbidden so backends MUST override.

(B) Extend apply_space_patch with new variants: AddInvite, RemoveInvite, AddBan, RemoveBan. Reuses the existing atomic-pre-validation pass on the Space body.

(C) Add may_create_space_ban / may_create_space_invite hooks (analogous to may_set_custom_emoji). Handlers call pre-flight. Backend create_object<SpaceBan>/create_object<SpaceInvite> additionally re-checks atomically.

Recommendation: Path A. Reasons:

1. SpaceBan and SpaceInvite are their own JmapObject types with /get, /changes, /set, /query handlers — they are siblings of Space, not nested children of Space. Path B is the wrong wire-shape: it would conflate "structural patch ops on the Space object" with "create/destroy of independent JmapObject types".

2. Path C requires the generic create_object/destroy_object<O: SetObject> to type-check the object and route SpaceBan/SpaceInvite through special gated paths. That re-check is type-erased over the generic O parameter and adds runtime type-dispatch inside the reference MemoryBackend. Messy.

3. Path A is the most direct expression of "the backend is canonical for this object family". The 4 methods cleanly enumerate the gated mutations. Default impl returning forbidden makes the kit fail-closed for any backend that does not opt in. The handler still uses the typed method, so the surface is small.

Cost of Path A: 4 new trait methods, 4 new MemoryBackend impls, 4 new impls each on FaultyBackend / IdentityBackend / TrackingBackend (12 method bodies in test scaffolding) — but most of those are 5-line forward-to-inner stubs.

Whichever path is chosen, both .3 and .4 should be done together to avoid inconsistent patterns. A defense-in-depth handler-side pre-check using the resolved principal_id + the appropriate permission constant is also needed under all three paths — that part is the same regardless.

Workspace policy implications: this would be the first add of multiple typed-by-object-type methods to ChatBackend (the existing typed paths are apply_space_patch and apply_space_metadata_patch which are per-method, not per-object). It would also be the precedent for analogous gates on any future per-object permission requirements that the chat draft adds.

Filed both .3 and .4 as human-labeled rather than pick Path A unilaterally because (i) the choice is between three plausible architectures the bead body did not rank, (ii) the change adds 4 trait methods plus default-forbidden semantics that are visible to every downstream consumer of jmap-chat-server, and (iii) doing this is the workspace pattern for similar gates on Calendars/Tasks/Contacts/etc. that will mimic whichever choice lands here.
